v.why: Adding the direct input-to-output residual path helps most when no 0->3 path exists at all, as in experiments 3-4 with gains up to +16 on IN16.
Replacing the residual skip with a conv removes the identity path and hurts (experiment 13), while filling an empty edge 3 helps (experiment 14).
Removing the input-output skip destroys the residual shortcut, which is the most damaging deletion in this space.
When edge 4 is absent, edge 5 carries most of the deep feature flow into the output, so swapping its conv for pooling hurts much more (experiments 15 vs 16).
Replacing the strongest op on the final edge with parameter-free pooling removes key learned capacity, which hurts more than replacing weaker ops.
Upgrading pooling to conv on the final edge gives a large gain (experiments 1-2), whereas the same edit applied to stronger ops gains little or nothing.
Deeper conv capacity on edge 5 is easier to exploit when a residual shortcut stabilizes training (experiment 1 vs 2).
Converting a pooling edge into the output to a 3x3 conv adds learnable capacity, unlike edits applied to edges that already hold convs.
An extra skip on edge 4 is redundant when the input-output residual already exists and only displaces a conv (experiments 19 vs 20).
With edge 2 missing, node 1 feeds fewer downstream paths, so changing edge 0 matters less (experiments 17 vs 18).
